Q: boto3 presigned PUT URL for Backblaze B2 S3 returns SignatureDoesNotMatch A:

Here’s a clear, technical StackOverflow-style answer you can post 👇

When generating presigned PUT URLs for Backblaze B2 S3-compatible API, SignatureDoesNotMatch is almost always caused by one of the following:

  1. Region mismatch

  2. Incorrect endpoint configuration

  3. Header mismatch between signing and request

  4. Virtual-host vs path-style mismatch

Backblaze B2 is S3-compatible, but not identical to AWS S3 — so configuration must be exact.

✅ 1. Use Correct Endpoint + Region Together

For B2 S3-compatible API, the region must match the endpoint exactly.

For your case:

  • Region: eu-central-003

  • Endpoint:
    https://s3.eu-central-003.backblazeb2.com

These must match in boto3 config.

✅ 2. Correct boto3 Configuration (IMPORTANT)

Use explicit signature version and path-style addressing:

import boto3
from botocore.config import Config

config = Config(
    signature_version='s3v4',
    s3={'addressing_style': 'path'}
)

client = boto3.client(
    's3',
    endpoint_url='https://s3.eu-central-003.backblazeb2.com',
    aws_access_key_id='YOUR_KEY_ID',
    aws_secret_access_key='YOUR_SECRET_KEY',
    region_name='eu-central-003',
    config=config
)

url = client.generate_presigned_url(
    ClientMethod='put_object',
    Params={
        'Bucket': 'your-bucket-name',
        'Key': 'test.txt',
    },
    ExpiresIn=600
)

print(url)

If region_name does not exactly match eu-central-003, signature will fail.

✅ 3. Do NOT Add Extra Headers in curl

If you generate the URL without specifying headers, then your PUT must also not include extra signed headers.

Correct minimal test:

curl -X PUT -T test.txt "PRESIGNED_URL"

Do NOT add:

  • Content-Type

  • x-amz-*

  • Host manually

If you add headers that were not part of the signing process, signature breaks.

✅ 4. If You Want to Send Content-Type

Then you must include it in the presign step:

url = client.generate_presigned_url(
    'put_object',
    Params={
        'Bucket': 'your-bucket-name',
        'Key': 'test.txt',
        'ContentType': 'text/plain'
    },
    ExpiresIn=600
)

And then:

curl -X PUT -T test.txt \
  -H "Content-Type: text/plain" \
  "PRESIGNED_URL"

Headers must match exactly.

✅ 5. Most Common B2-Specific Mistake

Backblaze requires:

  • Signature v4 only

  • Exact region match

  • Correct endpoint

  • Path-style addressing (important)

If you accidentally use:

  • Default AWS region (us-east-1)

  • Virtual host style

  • Wrong endpoint format

You will get SignatureDoesNotMatch.

✅ 6. Debug Tip

To confirm what is being signed:

Enable botocore logging:

import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)

Then inspect:

  • Canonical request

  • Signed headers

  • Credential scope (region must match)

🔎 Summary Checklist

✔ region_name == eu-central-003
✔ endpoint_url matches region
✔ signature_version = s3v4
✔ addressing_style = path
✔ No extra headers in curl
✔ Bucket name correct

When these align, Backblaze B2 presigned PUT works correctly.

Q: Why can't the returned object from CodeIgniter's row() method be printed with PHP's echo? A: 
$this->db->select('title')->from('entries')->where('id', 1);

Generates

SELECT title FROM entries WHERE id = 1

$query retrieves the result in an array:

array( [0] => array( [title] => 'your title' ))

row('title') returns the title column from the first row of your result array.

The reason you need to tell it which column to get is because row and get can be used with many columns.

Q: React rendering animations inconsistently for a back to front Carousel A:

This problem is specifically very frustrating in the world of 3d aniamtions, but however I have some experience with 3d carousel, as in this website I made: https://enterprise.integri.app/features
So here is my analysis, which you may find helpful, although i didnt get the proper reason because these things are better to understand when visualize so I hope you find this helpful :

1. The "Race Condition" Glitch (Overlapping & Stucking)

When you use React state or standard CSS to manage a sequence, each step is essentially independent.

  • The Problem: If a user scrolls or clicks too fast, the second animation starts before the first one finishes. In "pure code," these animations often fight over the same DOM properties. This leads to images "stucking" or "coming before the first ones" because the logic hasn't finished resetting the previous state.

  • The GSAP Solution: GSAP’s overwrite: "auto" or kill() properties automatically handle conflicting animations. If a new movement starts, GSAP cleanly stops the old one and takes over from the current position, preventing that "jittery" look.

2. Synchronization and the "Timeline" Concept

Building a timeline (especially for something like a career or project history) requires strict sequencing.

  • The Problem: In raw code, managing a sequence usually involves a messy chain of setTimeout or onTransitionEnd callbacks. If one image lags by even 50ms, the entire rest of the sequence is thrown off, causing the "glitching after 2 or 3 images" your friend is seeing.

  • The GSAP Solution: The gsap.timeline() object acts as a master controller. You can place animations at absolute or relative time-stamps. If the timeline pauses or skips, every single element stays perfectly synced because they are all bound to the same global ticker.

3. Performance Lag (Jank)

If the carousel is "glitchy" or lagging, it’s often because the code is triggering the browser's "Layout" engine too frequently.

  • The Problem: Standard JS animations that change properties like top, left, or width force the browser to recalculate the entire page layout. This is slow and causes frame drops.

  • The GSAP Solution: GSAP is optimized to prioritize "Composite" properties (like x, y, scale, and rotation). These are handled by the GPU rather than the CPU, which is why animations feel "buttery smooth" even on hardware that isn't top-of-the-line.

    Specific Advice for the 3D Carousel

    If the bottom of the carousel is hiding under other content or cards are behaving "weird," it’s likely a z-index or perspective issue. In a raw implementation, the browser doesn't always know which 3D card should be "on top" during a transition. GSAP handles the depth sorting much more gracefully by updating the translateZ and zIndex in a single high-speed pass.

Q: Multiple staging areas A:

(Disclosure: I'm the author of git-cl.)

git-cl addresses this at the file level rather than the patch level, so if your changes are separable by file, it removes the need to cycle through git add -p repeatedly:

git cl add bugfixes   solver.py utils.py
git cl add features   analysis.py plotting.py
git cl commit bugfixes -m "Fix convergence issues"
git cl commit features -m "Add analysis pipeline"

Each named changelist acts as an independent staging area. You assign files as you work, then commit each group when ready without touching the others.

If your changes are genuinely interleaved within the same file, git add -p remains the right tool. But for the common case of logically separate files, this avoids the repeated cycling.

Q: std::mersenne_twister_engine and range of values generated A:

is it correct to assume that this range is taken from the range prescribed for std::uniform_int_distribution?

No, w is simply the second template parameter:

template<
    class UIntType, std::size_t w, std::size_t n, std::size_t m, std::size_t r,
//                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    UIntType a, std::size_t u, UIntType d, std::size_t s,
    UIntType b, std::size_t t, UIntType c, std::size_t l, UIntType f
> class mersenne_twister_engine;

As seen in the two predefined specializations:

In std::mt19937, the second parameter is 32, resulting in the range [0, 232).

std::mersenne_twister_engine<std::uint_fast32_t,
                             32, 624, 397, 31,
                             0x9908b0df, 11,
                             0xffffffff, 7,
                             0x9d2c5680, 15,
                             0xefc60000, 18, 1812433253>

In std::mt19937_64, the second parameter is 64, resulting in the range [0, 264).

std::mersenne_twister_engine<std::uint_fast64_t,
                             64, 312, 156, 31,
                             0xb5026f5aa96619e9, 29,
                             0x5555555555555555, 17,
                             0x71d67fffeda60000, 37,
                             0xfff7eee000000000, 43,
                             6364136223846793005>

Q: Bash recursion bug with ghost item in array? A:

As an alternative to local:

You don't appear to be particularly concerned with performance (for example, invoking Perl twice just to do two substitutions is rather expensive), so you could guarantee that your functions have no side-effects in the caller by replacing braces with parentheses so that the function's commands are run in a subshell:

function recurse_directories {
    : ...
}

can become:

recurse_directories (
    : ...
)

Since you are already using Perl, you could rewrite all the bash as a single Perl program. This should remove most need for manual inter-language double-escaping.

For example, these:

local r="$(echo "$S" | perl -pe 's/\//\\\//g' | perl -pe 's/\./\\./g')\/[^\"]+"

local ls=($(curl -s "$S" | perl -lne "print for /$r/g" | sort | uniq))

might perhaps become:

my $r = qr{\Q$S\E/[^"]+};

use List::Util qw(uniq);
my @ls = sort uniq qx{curl -s \Q$S\E} =~ /$r/g;  # escape perl var

# or

use List::Util qw(uniq);
$ENV{'S'} = $S;
my @ls = sort uniq qx'curl -s "$S"' =~ /$r/g;    # sh uses envvar
